title: Finite discrete condensed coefficients and ordinary module sheaves
statement: Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring with its discrete condensed structure $\underline A$, and let $T$ be a scheme. Work on the small pro-étale site with the size and sheafification conventions of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules] and [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor]. The pulled-back ring object $p_T^*\underline A$ is isomorphic, as a ring object, to the constant ring sheaf $A_T$. The section-action equivalence of [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence] gives an exact equivalence between internal $p_T^*\underline A$-module objects and ordinary $A_T$-module sheaves. Its termwise extension is an equivalence of unbounded derived categories preserving relative derived tensor products and every Tor-amplitude interval [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude]. It identifies the finite constant local models and bounded constructible finite-Tor subcategories of [sk-def-sfb-constructible], and preserves shifts, distinguished triangles, and small coproducts, hence their localizing closures [sk-def-localizing-closure]. For every scheme morphism $f:X\to Y$ and fixed compactification $X\xrightarrow{j}\bar X\xrightarrow{p}Y$ of $f$, these equivalences identify the module-object composite $Rp_*D(j_!)$ of [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-lower-shriek] with the ordinary constant-$A$ module-sheaf composite $Rp_*j_!$ for that same compactification [def-sfb-finite-derived-lower-shriek-compactification].

source.place: Step 8, coefficient identification and exact derived equivalence between internal module objects and ordinary constant-ring sheaves.

proof.text: Choose the proved normalized Encoding for each scheme. Its ring isomorphism is normalized on constant sections, and both additive equivalences have the required exact forward functors.

Apply the separate tensor/Tor, constructibility and fixed-compactification comparisons. Widen a finite-Tor witness [a,b] to [min(a,b),b] in either direction; then the ordered-interval comparison proves finite-Tor equivalence. Combine with bounded constructibility to identify the two finite-Tor generating predicates.

The actual termwise derived equivalence and its inverse commute with shifts and are triangulated; equivalences preserve every existing coproduct. The fixed-scalar generating predicate is invariant under isomorphism: use the same covers and strata, the homology comparison, and Tor invariance. Pulling back any replete triangulated coproduct-closed property preserves those properties. Apply the two directions of the equivalence to the intersection defining localizingClosure and use unit/counit isomorphisms to obtain both implications.

proof_origin.note: Encoding, ordered-to-finite Tor glue, invariance under isomorphism, shifts/triangles/coproducts, and both directions of localizing-closure transport are complete Lean proofs. lean.statement: theorem moduleObject_ordinary_coefficient_equivalence [Finite A] [DiscreteTopology A] : ∃ E : ∀ T : Scheme.{u}, Encoding A T, (∀ T : Scheme.{u}, Nonempty ((E T).fixedDerived.functor.Monoidal) ∧ (∀ (K : DerivedCategory (Internal A T)) (a b : ℤ), a ≤ b → (DerivedCategory.torAmplitudeIn _ a b K ↔ Scheme.HasProEtaleTorAmplitude T A ((E T).ordinaryDerived.functor.obj K) a b)) ∧ (∀ (K : DerivedCategory (Internal A T)) (a b : ℤ), a ≤ b → (DerivedCategory.torAmplitudeIn _ a b K ↔ DerivedCategory.torAmplitudeIn _ a b ((E T).fixedDerived.functor.obj K))) ∧ (∀ M : Internal A T, HasFiniteConstantLocalModel (coefficient A) T M ↔ ordinaryLocalModel A T (((E T).ordinary.functor ⋙ (E T).fixed.functor).obj M)) ∧ (∀ K : DerivedCategory (Internal A T), (constantModelBoundedConstructible (coefficient A) T K ∧ DerivedCategory.finiteTorAmplitude _ K) ↔ ordinaryCtf A T ((E T).fixedDerived.functor.obj K)) ∧ Nonempty ((E T).fixedDerived.functor.CommShift ℤ) ∧ (E T).fixedDerived.functor.IsTriangulated ∧ PreservesColimitsOfSize.{u + 1, u + 1} (E T).fixedDerived.functor ∧ (∀ K : DerivedCategory (Internal A T), localizingClosureProEtale (coefficient A) T K ↔ CategoryTheory.localizingClosure (ordinaryCtf A T) ((E T).fixedDerived.functor.obj K))) ∧ (∀ (X Y : Scheme.{u}) (f : X ⟶ Y) (c : Compactification f), Nonempty (CondensedRing.rightDerivedLowerShriekOfCompactification (coefficient A) c ⋙ (E Y).fixedDerived.functor ≅ (E X).fixedDerived.functor ⋙ rightDerivedLowerShriekOfCompactification (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} A)) c))
lean.note: The canonical coefficient map is sheafified constant functions followed by the existing constantSchemeIso and upperStarFromPoint. Encoding fixes the ring isomorphism on every constant scalar and fixes both forward functors to section-action/scalar restriction. Its two derived equivalences are the actual termwise Equivalence.mapDerivedCategory, not independent equivalences. Tensor and compactification comparison use the equivalent fixed-ULift-A module-sheaf presentation; Tor intervals are also compared directly with the recorded intrinsic HasProEtaleTorAmplitude. The ordinary local-model and constructibility helpers render the ordinary side of this node with the same covers, strata and affine-local convention; they introduce no new independent notion or chosen data. The two definition nodes def-sfb-constant-ring-module-restriction and def-sfb-constant-sheaf-scheme-pullback-comparison own the existing canonical constructions used by the signature; the associated theorem nodes are proof dependencies. The recorded derived-constant-module interface is also a statement dependency. K1: the unchanged definitions and derived encoding constructions are now publicly re-exported from Sheaf.Paper.FiniteDiscreteOrdinaryEncoding, attached to lem-sf-finite-discrete-normalized-encoding.
